description.text:
Build the agents. Learn the platform. Two skill trees, one role.
We are an edge AI industrial computer (IPC) provider, and we are rebuilding how technical support works — not by hiring more people to answer tickets, but by building AI agents that do the repetitive work so engineers can focus on the hard problems. This is a junior role, but not an ordinary one: you are hired to help build that agent layer, while learning the edge-AI-IPC domain that makes the agents actually useful.
You don't need years of FAE experience. You need to be someone who, when they see a repetitive task, wants to automate it — and who is genuinely curious about how AI runs on real hardware at the edge. We'll teach you the domain; you bring the builder's instinct.
Why the two skill trees matter: an AI agent is only as good as the domain knowledge behind it. A ticket-triage agent that doesn't understand what a BSP is, or why a Jetson thermal-throttles, is useless. So you'll grow both at once — writing agents AND learning the platform they reason about.
What you'll do
◆Build and maintain AI agents in our support workflow — ticket auto-classification, knowledge-base retrieval (RAG), draft-response generation, and the automated test bench that turns debugging rules into executable checks.
◆Script against LLM APIs (Python + Anthropic / OpenAI SDK) and wire up tool-calling / MCP-style integrations that let agents act on real systems.
◆Learn the edge AI IPC domain hands-on: what our industrial computers do, how NVIDIA Jetson / x86 edge platforms are deployed, and the common failure modes customers hit — so the agents you build reason about real problems.
◆Continuously feed resolved cases back into the knowledge base — every fix you or the team makes becomes training signal for the agents.
◆Sit alongside senior FAEs as they debug real customer issues, turning their judgment into agent logic and test rules.
Requirements (no years-of-experience requirement)
◆STEM background, or equivalent self-taught proof — side projects, maker builds, GitHub, course records all count.
◆You already build with AI, not just chat with it — you've scripted against an LLM API, built a small agent/bot, automated something in your own workflow, or made a RAG demo. Show us. This is the one hard requirement.
◆Basic Python and comfort with the command line / Linux.
◆Follow-through: you finish what you start. Bring one real example of something you carried from zero to done — any field.
◆Genuine curiosity about hardware and edge computing — you want to understand the machine, not just the software on top of it.
Nice to have
◆Prompt engineering for structured / reliable LLM output; experience with LangChain, LlamaIndex, or agent frameworks.
◆Hands-on hardware (Arduino / Raspberry Pi / Jetson Nano — toy-level is fine), or any embedded Linux exposure.
◆Basic understanding of edge AI concepts: model deployment, inference, CUDA / TensorRT (even just from a course or side project).
◆Any record of carrying responsibility: led a project, shipped something people used.
◆Reading-level English (technical docs, code comments, customer tickets).
What we offer
◆A rare combination: you learn to build production AI agents AND gain deep edge-AI-IPC domain expertise — two of the most valuable skill trees in tech, at the same time.
◆A complete AI toolchain and a knowledge base that compounds — you build on a working system, not a blank page.
◆A growth path we can put in writing: contributing agents + handling L1 tickets in 3 months → owning an agent workflow + a platform specialty in 12 months → Senior AI/FAE hybrid track.
◆One-on-one senior mentorship on both the AI side and the hardware side.
